conventions.convention: R_S is the algebraic direct sum of integral virtual-character groups, including R(S_0)=Z; its multiplication is outer induction, which adds degrees, rather than same-rank tensor multiplication.
ch(f)=Σρ f(ρ)pρ/zρ initially has codomain Λ_C for arbitrary complex class functions; integrality on virtual characters is proved subsequently.
The complex Hall form is sesquilinear, linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second, with ⟨pρ,pσ⟩=δρσzρ.

Hardy classes use normalized Borel Haar measure of mass one on T=R/Z, identified with the unit circle. Countable choice is assumed; finite p includes 0<p<1 with a quasi-norm, and radial suprema include r=0.
b_a(z)=(conjugate(a)/|a|)(a-z)/(1-conjugate(a)z) for a≠0, while b_0(z)=z. Zeros are counted with multiplicity; an empty Blaschke product is 1.
K(z,ζ)=(ζ+z)/(ζ-z); S_μ=exp(-∫K dμ) and [h]=exp(∫K log h dm). The normalized factors have S_μ(0)>0 and [h](0)>0; unimodular constants are separate.

General zero-free inner representation and canonical factorisation explicitly assume full AC for their Herglotz supplier. The boundary, local measure-decomposition, Nevanlinna, Smirnov, and F. and M. Riesz arguments retain countable-choice assumptions.
N+ contains zero separately. For nonzero f it requires Nevanlinna membership and log|f|≤P[log|f*|]; the zero boundary logarithm is not treated as an L1 datum.
The faithful modular action is by PSL_2(Z), with determinant-one matrix representatives acting on the left by (aτ+b)/(cτ+d); Sτ=-1/τ and Tτ=τ+1.

Weights are integers and the transformation law is imposed for every SL_2(Z) representative, including -I; consequently odd-weight forms vanish. Holomorphy at the cusp means holomorphy in q=e^(2πiτ) at q=0.

The positively oriented truncated fundamental domain traverses its lower circular arc clockwise from ω to ω+1. Its contribution is πik/6; elliptic zero orders are measured upstairs and weighted by 1/2 or 1/3.
The modular discriminant is (E_4^3-E_6^2)/1728 and j=E_4^3/Δ, so j(i)=1728. This differs from the lattice discriminant g_2^3-27g_3^2.
Theta uses Q=e^(πiτ), with Q²=q. Its inversion multiplier is s(τ)=exp(½Log(τ/i)), positive on the positive imaginary axis; the transformation lemma assumes countable choice.
Half-period labels are e_1=wp(1/2), e_2=wp(τ/2), e_3=wp((1+τ)/2), and λ=(e_3-e_2)/(e_1-e_2). Γ(2) acts through its projective image after quotienting by ±I.
The lambda-domain assertion concerns the open quadrilateral |Re τ|<1, |τ±1/2|>1/2, whose image omits both closed rays (-∞,0] and [1,∞). The full quotient Y(2) instead maps onto C\{0,1}.

load_bearing.statement: Assume countable choice. For 0<p≤∞ and f∈H^p, including zero, finite nontangential boundary values f* exist almost everywhere and belong to L^p. For finite p, f_r→f* in L^p and the boundary and Hardy norms agree; at infinity the norms agree and convergence is weak-star against L1. For p≥1, f=P[f*]; its analytic H1 representing measure is f*m.
For even k and nonzero f∈M_k, ΣP ord_P(f)/ν_P+ord_∞(f)=k/12, with ν_P=2 at the class of i, 3 at the class of ω, and 1 elsewhere; the cusp order is the q-order.

ch:R_S→Λ is a degree-preserving Z-module isomorphism, preserves outer induction products and the unit, and is an isometry for the sesquilinear Hall form. Consequently it is a graded ring isomorphism, also after scalar extension to Q or C. No choice principle is used.
Under countable choice, every bounded holomorphic disc function f has a unique φ∈L∞ with f=P[φ], ||φ||∞=sup_D|f|, and nontangential limits φ almost everywhere within every cone. Zero is allowed.
Assume countable choice. Every nonzero f∈N(D) has finite nontangential limits f* almost everywhere and log|f*|∈L1; in particular f*≠0 almost everywhere.
For nonzero f∈H^p(D), 0<p≤∞, log|f(z)|≤P[log|f*|](z) for every z, with log 0=-∞; equality holds throughout for outer f.

Under countable choice every finite-valued countably additive complex Borel measure on T has finite total variation, which is a finite regular positive Borel measure. Zero is allowed; no Hahn or Jordan decomposition is required.
For every n≥0 and λ⊢n, the Young permutation character φ^λ satisfies ch(φ^λ)=h_λ∈Λ^n.

D={τ∈H:|Re τ|<1/2,|τ|>1} is a fundamental domain for PSL_2(Z), with only the stated T- and S-boundary identifications. Stabilizers in its closure are cyclic of order 2 at i and order 3 at ω and ω+1, and PSL_2(Z)=⟨S,T⟩.
E_2(γτ)=(cτ+d)²E_2(τ)-(6ic/π)(cτ+d) for every γ∈SL_2(Z), and E_2 is 1-periodic. In particular its S-law has a nonzero correction and E_2 is not modular of weight 2.

j descends to a biholomorphism X(1)→the Riemann sphere, taking the cusp to infinity with a simple pole. The quotient map, rather than the descended j-map, has local degrees 2 on the orbit of i, 3 on the orbit of ω, and 1 elsewhere.
If τ,τ'∈H and λ(τ)=λ(τ'), then τ'=γτ for some γ∈Γ(2); together with invariance, the fibres are exactly the Γ(2)-orbits.

concerns.concern: The enumeration-independence paragraph estimates the quotient of two finite products whose index sets contain a common prefix. On compact sets containing a prefix zero, the written quotient is initially 0/0. Cancel the common factors first, or explicitly use its holomorphic extension; the remaining tail factors are zero-free on the compact set once the prefix is sufficiently long. This closes the stated argument without changing the definition or conclusion.

alerts.finding: Opened because cex-divergent-blaschke-sum cites it in F5 and step 3.1. Its Statement says 'A⊆Ω be discrete with multiplicities m(a)∈N' and promises 'whose zero at each a∈A has order exactly m(a)'. Two qualifications need checking: N includes zero in this library, so Ω=D, A={0}, m(0)=0 contradicts the literal requirement of a zero of order zero; also topological discreteness alone allows A={1/n:n≥2}⊂D, whose accumulation at 0 prevents the promised nonzero holomorphic function by the identity theorem. The proof assumes absence of accumulation throughout Ω, not merely isolation of points of A. The cited [Lebl text](https://www.jirka.org/ca/ca.pdf), Theorem 8.2.7, printed pp. 205–206, explicitly requires no limit points in the open set; its complete relevant proof was read. If 'discrete' is intended to mean locally finite here, that convention needs stating. The owned consumer uses an ambiently locally finite set and multiplicity one, so these boundary cases do not invalidate its particular application.
